defect.why_it_fails_INV_8: entry is fetched via Repo.get(Entry, service_id) at the top of delete/1; referencing_active_definitions/2 then runs a sequential per-tenant-schema query loop before this line executes -- a real window in which another caller can delete the same row concurrently. Entry has no optimistic-lock field, so Repo.delete/1 matches on primary key alone: if the row is gone by the time this line runs, Repo.delete/1 raises Ecto.StaleEntryError, which this bare match cannot catch -- it crashes the calling process instead of returning a typed error. This is the exact pattern INV-8's own grep heuristic (`grep -rn "^\s*{:ok, .*} = " lib/letflow/`) is written to catch, and it touches external I/O (the DB) directly, so INV-8 applies regardless of whether a route exists yet on top of delete/1.
defect.precedent_in_this_codebase: lib/letflow/webhooks.ex:270, Letflow.Webhooks.delete/2, passes Repo.delete(subscription, prefix: prefix)'s result straight through a `with` chain rather than bare-matching it -- Letflow.ServiceCatalog.delete/1 deviates from that established pattern without justification.
defect.suggested_fix_not_prescriptive: Replace the bare match with a case/with that handles Repo.delete/1's actual {:ok, _} | {:error, Ecto.Changeset.t()} result. If a concurrent delete should be treated as a benign outcome, rescue/handle Ecto.StaleEntryError explicitly and translate it to {:error, :not_found}, consistent with get_for_tenant/2's and update_scope/2's own not-found handling -- but do not leave the crash-on-race path unhandled.
